000
FXUS66 KMTR 280822
AFDMTR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service San Francisco CA
1222 AM PST Sat Nov 28 2026

...New SHORT TERM, LONG TERM...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 1208 AM PST Sat Nov 28 2026

 - Moderate coastal flooding continues into the weekend

 - Unsettled weather returns Sunday into Monday with light to
   moderate rain and gusty winds expected

 - Additional rain and gusty winds return Tuesday through early
   Wednesday

&&

.SHORT TERM...
Issued at 1208 AM PST Sat Nov 28 2026
(Today and tonight)

Another round of fog is possible tonight across the North Bay 
Interior Valleys and along the delta. Webcams show some fog 
creeping up the Russian River towards Santa Rosa but it is not as 
thick or widespread as it was at this time last night. The main 
difference between Thursday night and tonight is that last night 
high clouds were just beginning to approach the coast but tonight 
they are already firmly in place. The 00Z Saturday OAK sounding 
reflects our current cloud set up. It shows fairly dry conditions 
across the lower half of the atmosphere before becoming moister 
above 400 mb (approx 25000 ft) - where the high clouds are. 
Comparatively, Friday's 00Z OAK sounding showed drier conditions 
across the upper levels of the atmosphere which correlated to the 
clearer skies we saw last night. Switching now to the surface, the
00Z soundings from Friday and Saturday are fairly similar in the 
lower levels of the atmosphere. The dewpoint depression 
(calculated by taking the difference between the surface 
temperature and the surface dewpoint) is a reflection of how much 
temperatures need to cool by in order to reach the surface 
dewpoint. The lower the dewpoint depression, the more likely you 
are to see fog develop. The higher the dewpoint depression, the 
less likely you are to see fog develop. Both soundings reported a 
surface dewpoint depression around 7C with RH over the lowest 
levels of the atmosphere around 24-26% at 00Z . Given the similar 
surface setups, the biggest threat to fog development overnight 
will be the high clouds entrenches over the Bay Area. Fog is still
likely but it will be patchier in nature and not as widespread. 
If you live in the North Bay Valleys or drive along the San Pablo 
Bay/Delta region, keep an eye out for a potential Dense Fog 
Advisory overnight. Remember if you encounter fog slow down, use 
your low beams, and allow extra time to reach your destination.

Another day of above normal temperatures continues Saturday thanks 
to upper level ridging over much of California. Expect high 
temperatures in the upper 60s to low 70s with slightly warmer 
temperatures across the higher elevations of the Santa Cruz 
Mountains and the Santa Lucia Range. Not anticipating any record 
high temperatures to be set tomorrow although a few sites will be 
close. Some of the closest sites are Redwood City and San Jose. 
Redwood City is forecast to reach a high of 71 on Saturday with the 
record high temperature being 72 from 1956. For San Jose there is a 
slightly larger gap to clear, the forecast high is 71 and the record 
high temperature is 74 from 1911. No monthly records are anywhere 
close to being threatened. Overnight low temperatures are also on
the warmer side with morning lows in the 40s to low 50s. A quick 
comparison to climate data shows that our overnight temperatures 
are running about 5 to 10 degrees above normal for this time of 
year. High temperatures drop, becoming more seasonal, into the 
60s by Sunday as a pattern change begins.

Unsettled weather returns Sunday as we see a low pressure system
move along the Northern California coast before it tracks 
northwards towards the Pacific Northwest. Given the northerly 
track of the low, the Bay Area is only being clipped by the 
main moisture plume. Precipitation totals have improved (gone up) 
compared to yesterday with the highest totals remaining centered 
on the North Bay. For the North Bay we expect between 0.75-1.25", 
for the Santa Lucia Range and Santa Cruz Mountains between 
0.5-1.00", and for the rest of the Bay Area and Central Coast we 
expected between 0.25-0.5". This is considered beneficial rain 
with only nuisance flooding from ponding on roadways and in low 
lying areas expected. Winds strengthen Sunday with gusts largely 
between 25-35 mph but up to 40 mph in the windiest areas during
the day. Gale force gusts are possible along the nearshore marine
environments and within the San Pablo, San Francisco, and 
Monterey Bays. There is a 10-20% chance of thunderstorms across 
the North Bay from about 10 AM to 10 PM Sunday. Conditions align 
the best for thunderstorm development from around 1 PM through 7 
PM where there is about 200-300 J/kg of MUCAPE, conditionally 
unstable lapse rates between 6-7 C/km, and good low level speed 
shear (increasing wind speeds with height). The K-index suggests 
scattered thunderstorms are likely across the North Bay with the 
potential for isolated thunderstorms across the rest of the Bay 
Area Sunday afternoon. Confidence is lower in thunderstorm 
development outside of the North Bay given that not much
instability can be found outside of the North Bay.

&&

.LONG TERM...
Issued at 1208 AM PST Sat Nov 28 2026
(Sunday through Friday)

Light rain continues Sunday night into Monday before another round 
of rain arrives Tuesday. A low pressure system will approach 
California on Tuesday before moving southwards along the coastline 
and eventually moving into Southern California. The bulk of the 
moisture is pointed at Southern California but we will be clipped
by the edge of the edge of it. The focus for this system is on 
the Central Coast with between 0.5-1.00" expected across interior 
Monterey/San Benito, 0.25-0.5" across the coastal Monterey Bay, 
and up to 0.25" across the rest of the Bay Area. If the center of 
the low continues to shift southwards, we may see further 
reductions in rainfall totals. Expect another round of gusty 
winds during the day on Tuesday continuing into early Wednesday. 
Coastal areas and the higher elevations will experience the 
strongest winds as the main low level jet stays just offshore. 
Conditions will be borderline for a Wind Advisory along the coast.
There is a 5-10% chance of thunderstorms during the day on 
Tuesday but confidence is low at this time.

Tuesday night into Wednesday, expect strong offshore winds across 
the North Bay Interior Mountains across the Vaca Mountains and 
across the interior East Bay (Altamont Pass region). Gusts between
40 to 60 mph will be possible across favored mountain gaps and
passes and across the highest ridgelines. Not expecting any fire 
concerns with these offshore winds given how wet these areas have 
been recently. Subsequent rounds of moderate offshore winds are 
possible Wednesday Night into Thursday and Thursday Night into 
Friday but winds should be weaker. 

Seasonal temperatures continue through the long term forecast with 
high temperatures peaking in the 50s to low 60s. Overnight 
temperatures cool into the 30s to 40s across the region but not 
seeing any widespread potential for Cold Weather Advisory's to be 
needed. Long range guidance continues to resolve light, 
beneficial showers potentially arriving Friday into the weekend. 
Confidence is still on the lower end for any late week rain given
that models are still all over the place for this weekend. Expect
periods of hazardous beach conditions this week as incoming 
systems bring renewed chances for long period NW swell to arrive. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 903 PM PST Fri Nov 27 2026

VFR conditions with high clouds and light to gentle flow, generally 
offshore, at present. Low to moderate confidence of fog and stratus 
development at the North Bay and interior East Bay valleys 
overnight, with high cloud cover limiting the opportunity for 
overnight cooling and large scale offshore flow also complicating 
the forecast. Light to gentle offshore winds resume Saturday 
afternoon. Saturday night, close to and after the end of the TAF 
period, MVFR-IFR stratus approaches the coast ahead of an incoming 
storm system.

Vicinity of SFO... Moderate to high confidence of VFR through the 
TAF period with some mist possible Saturday morning. Winds remain 
light and gentle, generally from the north to the northeast. 
Moderate confidence of MVFR-IFR stratus developing Saturday night 
ahead of a storm system on Sunday after the end of the TAF period.

SFO Bridge Approach... Similar to SFO. 

Monterey Bay Terminals... VFR through Saturday evening. Offshore 
drainage flow overnight into Saturday morning before light to gentle 
offshore flow resumes in the afternoon. Saturday night, winds turn 
westerly and MVFR stratus approaches the terminals, although impacts 
to the terminals may not happen before the end of the TAF period.

&&

.MARINE...
(Tonight through next Thursday)
Issued at 903 PM PST Fri Nov 27 2026

Northerly breezes will continue through Saturday morning before
becoming southerly Saturday afternoon out ahead of the next
impactful system that will bring increased rain chances beginning
late Saturday night and continue through Tuesday with a slight
chance of thunderstorms across the northern waters Sunday
afternoon and evening. Expect moderate to rough seas in excess of
15 feet and developing long period swell over 15 seconds Tuesday
and Wednesday.

&&

.BEACHES...
Issued at 1241 AM PST Fri Nov 27 2026

The combination of king tides, storm surge, and thermal expansion
from warm El Nino waters will bring coastal flooding along the
bayshore and portions of the Pacific Coast, despite lower 
astronomical tides and limited wind- driven transport helping to 
lessen the expected tidal levels from what we saw over the last 
few days.

A Coastal Flood Advisory is in effect for bayshore locations 
along the San Francisco, San Pablo, and southern Monterey Bays 
through 5 PM Sunday. A Coastal Flood Advisory is in effect until 
4 PM Saturday for the Pacific Coast. At the San Francisco tidal 
gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft 
MLLW) at 1:28 PM Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) 
at 2:32 PM Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific 
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

A Beach Hazards Statement remains in effect through 6 AM Saturday due
to increased risk of sneaker waves, strong rip currents, and 
breaking waves between 13 to 19 feet. These conditions will 
coincide with King Tides and up to 1.3 ft of surge, bringing 
water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting 
escape from beaches and coastal areas. Large breaking waves can 
overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, 
jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and 
increasing the risk of drowning. Inexperienced swimmers should 
remain out of the water. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other 
waterside infrastructure and never turn your back on the ocean! 

Additional rounds of hazardous beach conditions are possible next
week as the storm door remains open.

&&

.MTR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
CA...Beach Hazards Statement until 6 AM PST early this morning for 
     CAZ006-505-509-529-530.

     Coastal Flood Advisory until 5 PM PST Sunday for CAZ006-506-508-
     530.

     Coastal Flood Advisory until 4 PM PST this afternoon for CAZ505-
     509-529.

PZ...Small Craft Advisory until 3 AM PST early this morning for 
     Pigeon Pt to Pt Pinos 10-60 NM-Pt Arena to Pt Reyes 10-60 
     NM.

&&

$$

nws_alerts.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 27 at 2:53PM PST until November 29 at 5:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
nws_alerts.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.7 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along San Pablo and San Francisco
Bays.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM
Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM
Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
